cap_confirmation: Resolved levels: Castform (+1) L53, Sawsbuck (+1) L53, Charizard (0) L52, Emolga (+2) L54 = cap 54 + offset - 2 on Medium.

attempts.why: Fake Out denied Sunny Day on turn 1. On turn 2 the AI switched its Mega ace Charizard directly into an already-committed Icicle Crash and lost it for free (see AI defect). Flare Blitz plus Icicle Crash then removed Sawsbuck, and Mega Gardevoir's Hyper Voice closed on Emolga. Lost only Mamoswine, to a sun-boosted Chlorophyll Horn Leech.

strategy_checks.check: Castform sets Sunny Day and Forecast transforms
strategy_checks.evidence: a1 turn 2: 'The sunlight turned harsh!' followed immediately by 'The opposing Castform transformed!'. Sun persisted for the rest of the battle.

strategy_checks.check: Castform cashes the sun with Weather Ball or Solar Beam
strategy_checks.evidence: Knock Off removed its Focus Sash and KOed it on the same turn the sun went up.

strategy_checks.check: Sawsbuck exploits Chlorophyll under the sun
strategy_checks.evidence: a1 turn 3: doubled Speed let Sawsbuck move before Mamoswine and Horn Leech OHKOed it (180) while healing back the Life Orb chip. This is the fight's one genuinely dangerous turn.

strategy_checks.check: Mega Charizard X Dragon Dance setup behind the sun
strategy_checks.evidence: Charizard entered on turn 2 by a mid-turn switch and fainted before acting, without Mega Evolving or using Dragon Dance. See AI defect E0277-1. The ace contributed nothing.

strategy_checks.check: Emolga's Lightning Rod redirects Electric moves
strategy_checks.evidence: I deliberately benched Regieleki and never selected an Electric move, so the redirection was never exercised. Recorded as untested rather than failed - the ability is correct on paper and the threat did change my party order, which is itself a design win.

strategy_checks.check: Emolga Encore locks a committed move
strategy_checks.evidence: a1 turn 4: Encore landed on Incineroar. It came one turn too late to matter but the selection was correct.

protect_ledger.payoff: blocked a 2x Icicle Crash that was close to lethal on a 164 HP Life Orb body - a correct read of the Ice threat on turn 1

empty - both of my moves were aimed at Sawsbuck. Defensible on expected value at 140/140 facing a Fire and an Ice attacker, but it produced nothing and Emolga then had to face the whole remaining party alone.

protect_summary: 2 opponent Protects, 1 with a real payoff, 1 empty but defensible. Not repetitive.

ai_defects.board: Sawsbuck L53 164/164 active alongside Castform L53 116/154. Facing Mamoswine, which had selected Icicle Crash at Sawsbuck on the previous turn (it was Protected) and was plainly the Ice threat on the field, and Incineroar.
ai_defects.chosen: Withdrew Sawsbuck and sent in Charizard L52, the team's Mega ace, into the incoming attack.
ai_defects.outcome: 'Mamoswine used Icicle Crash! The opposing Charizard fainted!' Charizard was removed from the game before it could Mega Evolve or Dragon Dance even once. The whole SETUP half of this team's authored strategy died on that switch.
ai_defects.better_action: Keep Sawsbuck in and attack, or Protect again, or switch to Emolga, whose Flying typing is no worse into Ice and which is not the ace. Switching the single most valuable member, at the lowest level on the team, into a slot that a revealed Ice attacker was pointed at is the worst available option. This looks like the switch evaluator scoring the incoming Pokemon's matchup against the field without charging it the damage it will eat on the switch-in turn.
ai_defects.note: Reported only. No AI C code was touched. This pattern would affect any team whose Mega or ace is held in reserve, so it is worth tracing as shared switch-scoring behaviour rather than a Kayley-only issue.

level_change_rationale: Keep, deliberately, against the surface reading. This was a first-attempt win in three turns with one faint, which normally triggers +1 to the weakest members. But the reason it was a three-turn win is that the AI threw away its Mega ace on a switch (defect E0277-1), so this battle's real difficulty at these levels has not actually been measured. Per the repository rule that AI defects are fixed before levels compensate for them, raising Castform or Sawsbuck now would be paying for an AI bug with numbers. Sawsbuck under its own sun already OHKOed a 200 HP Mamoswine, which is the right amount of pressure for the slot.
cooler: Keep. Castform is a genuinely charming weather engine and Forecast plus Sunny Day plus a Chlorophyll partner is a clean, readable concept, while Emolga's Lightning Rod is doing real work simply by existing - it changed my party order before the fight started. One concrete improvement: Castform is the whole sun plan, carries a Focus Sash, and dies the instant anything Knocks the Sash off, so the sun lasted five turns of which the team used one. Giving Charizard the Charizardite Y instead of X would let the ace set its own sun on entry and make the plan survive Castform's death; if X is wanted for the Dragon Dance identity, Heat Rock on Castform at least buys the eight-turn window the rest of the team is built around.
legality_notes: No legality problem in the authored set.
verification_limit: No level change was made for this battle. It is however the battle in my block most worth replaying after AI defect E0277-1 is fixed, because the ace has never actually been fought.
